title: Ulyana and the Songbook
premise: Ivo Thornbury, a once-celebrated cellist whose hands failed him during a televised final performance, has spent three years hiding in a coastal town, teaching beginners and avoiding the piano teacher next door—Ulyana Voss, the woman who wrote him anonymous letters of encouragement for a decade under the name 'A. Song.' When Ulyana inherits her late aunt's house and moves in beside him, Ivo realizes the letters he treasured came from the one person he pushed away after their conservatory romance collapsed. As they restore her aunt's water-damaged songbook together, Ivo discovers his former manager engineered both his breakdown and their breakup to keep control of his career—and that Ulyana is losing her hearing, racing to finish transcribing the songbook before silence takes it. At the songbook's completion concert, Ivo returns to the stage not as the virtuoso he was but as her accompanist, choosing love and imperfect music over the corrupted career that saved everything except him.
about_author: Ansel Reyes is a former music critic from Portland who writes romances about artists learning to fail beautifully. Their work has appeared in several small literary journals, though this is their first novel.

chapters.title: The Last Note That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, three years after his catastrophic final performance. He teaches a nervous ten-year-old cello student, flinching at every wrong note as if it were his own. A moving truck arrives at the neighboring cottage. The emotional beat: grief disguised as routine, and the first tremor of disruption when he glimpses a familiar silhouette unloading boxes.

chapters.title: Letters from A. Song
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Unpacking, he finds his shoebox of letters signed 'A. Song'—a decade of anonymous encouragement beginning at the conservatory. When Ulyana Voss knocks to borrow a ladder, he nearly drops it; she left him years ago without explanation. They exchange brittle civilities. Emotional beat: shock curdling into old resentment, the past refusing its past tense.

chapters.title: The Water-Damaged Songbook
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She reveals she inherited her aunt Halina's cottage and a mold-stained songbook of original compositions, half-illegible. She asks Ivo—he alone can read the notation—to help reconstruct it. He refuses coldly. Alone, she confesses to the reader (not him) that she was A. Song. Emotional beat: longing on her side, pride wounded on his.

chapters.title: What the Manager Knew
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. His ex-manager Marcus arrives uninvited, dangling a comeback tour: 'the great redemption narrative.' Ivo notices Marcus flinches at mention of Ulyana. Flashback fragments reveal Marcus orchestrated the conservatory breakup with a forged letter. Emotional beat: suspicion awakening; the reader sees power tightening its grip while Ivo still trusts it.

chapters.title: Duets for One Good Ear
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ulyana admits her degenerative hearing loss; she needs Ivo's ear to finish the songbook before hers fails. He agrees—not forgiveness, but a bargain. Working sessions become charged: her hand over his on the page, arguments about phrasing that are really about everything else. Emotional beat: reluctant intimacy, collaboration as courtship.

chapters.title: Halina's Margins
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In the songbook's margins they find Halina's notes—compositions written for a lover she never married, plus a letter revealing Halina once chose career over love and regretted it for fifty years. Ivo recognizes himself. Meanwhile Marcus calls: sign the tour or lose the rights to his own recordings forever. Emotional beat: the mirror of inheritance; two legacies, two choices.

chapters.title: The Forged Letter
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She finds the original of the letter that ended their relationship—in Halina's papers, because Marcus had used Halina's typewriter and stationery decades ago when managing them both. Confronting Ivo, she shows him the proof. His decade of blame collapses. Emotional beat: devastation transformed into fury, then tenderness—the truth arriving almost too late.

chapters.title: Ringing Ears
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ulyana suffers a sudden worsening episode; sounds begin smearing. Terrified, she pushes Ivo away—'finish it without me'—repeating his own old pattern. He refuses to leave, playing the reconstructed pieces directly against her cheekbone so she can feel them. Emotional beat: role reversal; now he must be the one who stays visible and stubborn.

chapters.title: The Contract on the Table
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Marcus offers a final deal: the tour, full rights restored—but Ivo must publicly disavow the songbook project as amateur work and cut Ulyana out entirely. Ivo signs nothing, instead leaking evidence of Marcus's old sabotage to the press. Emotional beat: climax of the power theme; Ivo burns the career that saved everything except him.

chapters.title: Everything We Could Hear
chapters.summary: Final chapter, alternating POV converging. In Halina's garden, a small concert: Ivo performs the completed songbook publicly for the first time since his collapse, with Ulyana conducting by touch and feeling the music through the ground and his back. Her hearing is mostly gone; she hears it anyway. Epilogue beat: the songbook published under both names, love in present tense at last.
